description.value: Study for an illustration for a Knopf edition (unpublished) of Carl Van Vechten's controversial novel, N***** Heaven, originally published in 1926. Two figures, abstractly rendered, facing one another. The figure on the left is depicted standing, and wearing a long red robe or dress. The figure on the right appears to be in a seated position, and is dressed in black. The figure in red raises one hand above the head of the figure in black. Yellow brushstrokes suggest the background surrounding the two figures.

legal.credit: Gift of Mrs. E. McKnight Kauffer

At center, the face of a woman [the character Adora Boniface] wearing a blue pearl necklace and matching blue pearl earrings, looking to the left. description.value: Illustration for Frederick Edwin Smith’s book, The World in 2030 A.D., for which Kauffer produced a series of drawings using an airbrush technique. At bottom, two rows of people sit in chairs watching a presenter, standing in front of them. The standing figure points to a large presentation screen above. On the screen, a depiction of an artist mannequin running to the right, and a note on the diagram at upper left that reads: Chart A / Movement.

inscription.markings: Stamped in purple ink, on verso: BOOK ILLUSTRATION, / BY E. McKNIGHT KAUFFER.

legal.credit: Gift of Mrs. E. McKnight Kauffer

description.value: Study of a motif, featuring an abstract figure comprised of geometric shapes. The figure’s head, at top, is a brown circle, connected to the body by a graphite outline of a neck.
